candidates: When building an absolute-positioned overlay (e.g. a suffix mask `div`) that must visually align with text inside a styled `<input>`, offset the overlay's `left` to match the input's horizontal padding as defined in the shared `Form/styles.ts`; do not leave the overlay at `left: 0` while the input text starts further right. To stay in sync without hardcoding, extract the padding value into a shared constant or CSS variable referenced by both the input style definition in `styles.ts` and the overlay.

When writing boolean conditions that combine multiple equality checks with `||`, ensure every disjunct is a complete comparison expression — `a === b || c` where `c` is a truthy variable is NOT equivalent to `a === b || a === c`. Always write out the full comparison on each side of `||` (and `&&`) to avoid silent operator-precedence bugs.

When adding non-editable informational elements (e.g. unit or suffix labels) adjacent to an `<input>`, give the element a stable `id` using `useId` from `@react-aria/utils` and link it to the input via `aria-describedby={suffixId}` so screen readers announce the extra context when the field receives focus.
